title: Performance knowledge: justify low-selectivity fields in key columns
summary: New performance guidance for justifying low-selectivity fields in table keys, requiring evidence such as filtered reads or skewed distributions before including Boolean, Option, or status fields in key columns.
key_points: Adds burden-of-proof rule for low-selectivity fields in keys to prevent over-indexing
Includes bad and good code examples showing a key with unfiltered leading flag being rewritten by ModifyAll
Requires evidence like equality filters on rare values, SIFT keys, unique combinations, or usage data
Performance review workflow now checks new or changed keys for Boolean, Option, Enum, or status fields
Applies to all BC versions with guidance on IncludedFields requirement for runtime 8.0+
quote: A low-selectivity or process-mutated key column needs a named read and evidence
